ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: The Versatile History of Indians in Latin America. Description: How can we write the history of the indigenous people of Latin America from the colonial period to the modern era? This question has vexed generations of historians and they have found different ways of writing about the origins of Indians from Meso- and South America, their cultures, and their adaptations to new cultural influences. By reading the most outstanding of these historians, we want to analyze how Western concepts of indegenes have changed over time. Whenever we can, we also consult native peoples' own historiographies. By doing so, we are induced to reflect our own historical methods. How do we construct objectivities? How do we interpret the history of indigenous societies? This class will thus introduce you to both: Latin American historiographies with a particular focus on native people as well as a discussion about our own historical methods.
